blueprint.name: Apologia Sancta Complete Curriculum and Prerequisite Blueprint
blueprint.authorityStatement: A structural curriculum proposal ordered to Catholic teaching; it is not itself a Magisterial document and requires named human approval before lesson production.

governance.centre: Jesus Christ and the mystery of the Trinity
governance.hierarchyOfTruths: The curriculum gives compulsory priority to the Trinity, Incarnation, Paschal Mystery, Church, grace, sacramental life, moral discipleship, and prayer before specialist disputes.
governance.approvalPolicy: All records remain draft and unpublished. Lesson production begins only after structural, theological, licensing, graph-taxonomy, and volume approvals.

sourceTypes: Code of Canon Law or Eastern canon law
Peer-reviewed scientific source or consensus statement

prerequisiteArchitecture.rule: A group unlocks when every configured prerequisite group has mastery at or above the threshold. Thresholds are data, not hard-coded application logic.

learnerRoutes.name: Convert or Catechumen Route
learnerRoutes.rule: Complete the compulsory route in order, then branch according to catechetical needs and local formation.

learnerRoutes.name: Catholic Deepening Route
learnerRoutes.rule: Use a diagnostic to recognise prior formation, but require mastery evidence before skipping a core group.

learnerRoutes.name: Apologist Route
learnerRoutes.rule: Complete foundations, source evaluation, one comparative specialism, and the independently reviewed Apologist Lab.

learnerRoutes.name: Casual Quiz Route
learnerRoutes.rule: Permit practice-only previews after the first foundations group; previews do not confer mastery or unlock advanced doctrinal production.

learnerRoutes.name: Independent Bible-Book Route
learnerRoutes.rule: After Scripture and Canon distinctions, choose any biblical book independently; no book requires completion of another book.

programmes.name: Compulsory Catholic Foundation Route
programmes.description: A Christ-centred entry route through revelation, Scripture, salvation history, Trinity, Christ, Church, grace, sacraments, moral life, and prayer before specialist branching.
learningOutcomes: Give a coherent Christ-centred account of Catholic faith
Navigate the Catechism's Creed, Sacraments, Moral Life, and Prayer
Distinguish doctrinal authority levels
Use Scripture, Tradition, and Magisterium together
Enter specialist tracks with the required prior concepts

programmes.name: Dogma and Sacramental Theology
programmes.description: Advanced parallel study of God, Trinity, Christ, redemption, grace, sacraments, Eucharist, and Christian hope.
learningOutcomes: Explain central dogmas with technical precision
Integrate biblical, patristic, conciliar, and philosophical evidence
Answer major sacramental and salvation disputes
Relate doctrine to liturgy and spiritual life
requiredPriorConcepts: mastery of the compulsory Catholic foundation route or specified gateway

programmes.name: Church, Tradition, and History
programmes.description: Parallel specialist formation in ecclesiology, succession, papacy, liturgy, Mary, saints, history, Fathers, councils, and heresies.
learningOutcomes: Explain the Church's visible and spiritual constitution
Use early and conciliar sources responsibly
Distinguish development from corruption
Address authority and Marian disputes without overstatement
requiredPriorConcepts: mastery of the compulsory Catholic foundation route or specified gateway

programmes.name: Moral and Spiritual Formation
programmes.description: Parallel formation in moral reasoning, conscience, virtue, bioethics, marriage, prayer, spiritual traditions, and Catholic social teaching.
learningOutcomes: Reason from beatitude, dignity, virtue, and moral object
Form conscience within truth and grace
Apply principles to contested cases with pastoral care
Develop a stable sacramental and prayer life
requiredPriorConcepts: mastery of the compulsory Catholic foundation route or specified gateway
requiredSourceTypes: Peer-reviewed scientific source or consensus statement

programmes.name: Reason, Philosophy, and Contemporary Culture
programmes.description: Parallel formation in philosophy, natural theology, evil, science, secularism, debate, and source evaluation.
learningOutcomes: Construct valid and proportionate arguments
Distinguish philosophical, theological, historical, and scientific claims
Engage unbelief and suffering honestly
Verify sources and communicate uncertainty
requiredPriorConcepts: mastery of the compulsory Catholic foundation route or specified gateway

programmes.name: Comparative Apologetics
programmes.description: Tradition-specific comparison with Protestant, Orthodox, Jewish, Islamic, world-religion, and new-religious-movement claims.

Distinguish internal variations
Build claim-specific Catholic responses
Practise dialogue ordered to truth, freedom, and charity
requiredPriorConcepts: mastery of the compulsory Catholic foundation route or specified gateway

programmes.name: Independent Bible-Book Studies

learningObjectives: Explain revelation: difficult texts and interpretive questions accurately in the context of Revelation.
Distinguish the key terms, authority levels, and claims needed for this topic.
Use the assigned source categories proportionately and identify claims needing reviewer verification.

catechism.name: The Celebration of the Christian Mystery (Sacraments)

disputes.name: Grace, faith, works, merit, and assurance
Purgatory and prayer for the dead
Logical and evidential problems of evil
God, morality, meaning, and religious harm
Economics, politics, war, migration, and ecology
Trinity, Incarnation, Crucifixion, and Gospel integrity in Islam
Uniqueness of Christ, salvation, and interreligious dialogue

intentionalOverlaps.rationale: The compulsory route teaches the creed-level whole; specialist subjects add technical distinctions and objections.
The compulsory route remains Christ-centred while specialist study separates person and saving work.
Foundational ecclesial-sacramental literacy precedes dispute-specific depth.
All learners receive the moral and prayer pillars before advanced cases or spiritual schools.

gaps.description: The current graph taxonomy has no dedicated categories for sacraments generally, moral theology, prayer, liturgy, social teaching, bioethics, Church Fathers, councils, or most biblical books.
gaps.disposition: Keep empty or nearest-category links in draft; require graph-taxonomy approval before lesson production.

gaps.description: No repository policy identifies approved Bible translations, quotation limits, territories, or APK/offline redistribution terms.
gaps.disposition: Phase 4 must store references and original paraphrases until a written licensing policy is approved.

gaps.description: The existing editorial workflow validates quiz Question records, not the complete structured lesson-block model assumed by Phase 4.
gaps.disposition: Approve and implement the lesson block schema and revision workflow before full lesson bodies are imported.

gaps.description: Named qualified reviewers for Orthodox, Islamic, Jewish, world-religion, NRM, science, bioethics, and abuse-sensitive material are not yet assigned.
gaps.disposition: Assign reviewers and escalation rules before those lesson batches move beyond draft.

gaps.description: The blueprint does not presume staff competence in Greek, Hebrew, Latin, Syriac, Arabic, or other source languages.
gaps.disposition: Record translation editions and require specialist review when an argument turns on original-language claims.

approvalsRequiredBeforeLessonProduction: Approve programme, subject, group, and prerequisite architecture.
Approve doctrinal classification vocabulary and review-risk assignments.
Approve lesson, practice, mastery, and study-time estimates.
Approve Apologia Graph taxonomy extensions and canonical link format.
Approve Scripture translation, quotation, territory, web, mobile, APK, and offline licensing policy.
Approve structured lesson-block schema and lesson-specific immutable review workflow.
Assign named Catholic, historical, scientific, and comparative-tradition reviewers.
Approve casual-player preview rules and expert-challenge gates.
Approve the database target mapping before executing any import.
